title: Taiping Heavenly Kingdom
capsule: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom (太平天國) was a millenarian Christian theocracy proclaimed by Hong Xiuquan, who believed himself the younger brother of Jesus Christ, after his movement captured Nanjing in March 1853 and renamed it Tianjing (Heavenly Capital). At its height the Taiping state controlled much of the Yangtze valley from Hubei to Jiangxi and held Nanjing for eleven years, with a population under its authority estimated in the tens of millions. The movement was suppressed by Qing forces augmented by the Ever-Victorious Army under Frederick Townsend Ward and later Charles Gordon; Nanjing fell in July 1864 after Hong Xiuquan died of illness, and the resulting death toll — from combat, famine, and disease — has been estimated at 20–30 million.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Taiping territorial control of the Nanjing region and lower Yangtze is well-documented by contemporaneous Western and Chinese sources, though peripheral zones of nominal allegiance versus effective control are difficult to demarcate.
